text.p: Acting U.S. Trade Representative Charlene Barshefsky said on Sunday that progress was being made on an information technology agreement, but it was too soon to say whether final agreement will be reached at the World Trade Organisation meeting this week.

"We are making very important progress," Barshefsky told reporters. She said U.S. and European officials held a round of technical discussions on Sunday to try to work out differences that remain and that U.S. officials would be meeting thoughout the week with officials from other countires in hopes of winning the final agreement at this week's meeting of World Trade Organisations ministers.
She said the United States was working the issue "delegation by delegation".
Barshefsky expressed concern about Europe's commitment to the agreement, which would eliminate tariffs on a wide range of computer and telecommunication products by 2000.

Specifically she said she was concerned about statements by European officials that indicated Europe felt completion of the ITA hinged upon the entirety of the declaration to be issued by WTO minister at the conclusion of this week's meeting. She added that she saw no linkage between the ITA and the WTO declaration.
